nodes.title: Eight-operation contract
nodes.say: Clients reach an installed app through a public contract of eight operations: capabilities, data queries and mutations, action runs, composition, cancellation and entity changes.

nodes.title: What happens with an app
nodes.say: An app's life has three paths here: installing a new package, running one of its actions, or reading and changing its stored data. Pick the one to follow.
nodes.decidedBy: which App Platform route the client calls: the owner package-import route, the public LaunchAction route, or the public QueryData / MutateData routes

options.label: Install a new app package
options.say: An owner uploads a package, reviews what it asks for, and grants only what they tick.

options.label: Run an installed app's action
options.say: A client launches one of the app's actions, and the app's agent works it as a durable task.

options.label: Query or change its data
options.say: A client reads or writes the app's own records directly, with no agent and no model call involved.

nodes.title: Upload app package
nodes.say: An owner uploads an app package, and the server checks its manifest and stages the bytes without granting the app any authority yet.

nodes.title: Installation review
nodes.say: Before install, a review lists every tool the app locks, how each one would run, and which hosts it declares or could reach.

nodes.title: Owner grants authority
nodes.say: The owner ticks exactly which tools, secrets, behaviors and hosts the app gets, and anything left unticked is simply denied.

nodes.title: Secrets scoped to hosts
nodes.say: Each secret is granted for one tool at a time and scoped to the hosts the owner picked, so a key only travels where allowed.

nodes.title: Registry commits install
nodes.say: The registry commits the reviewed grant, schema and surface in one transaction, advancing the installation and appending its outbox event together.

nodes.title: App installed
nodes.say: The app is installed with exactly the authority the owner approved, and every later run is checked against that grant.

nodes.title: Launch action route
nodes.say: A client launches an action by posting to the public runs route; the server checks the session and answers with an opaque run handle.

nodes.title: Admitted as a durable task
nodes.say: The workflow service stamps the current installation, grant and schema evidence, then admits the run as a durable app task under an idempotency key.

nodes.title: Tools narrowed to the grant
nodes.say: When the task runs, its tool list is cut down to the granted tools plus a store query tool and a terminal commit tool.

nodes.title: Model context admitted
nodes.say: The run's prompt is rendered from reviewed material and fenced by a disclosure guard that every model request of this run must carry.

nodes.title: Agent picks a tool
nodes.say: The app's agent answers with a tool call, and the executor treats it as a protected app tool rather than an ordinary one.

nodes.title: Bind and contain check
nodes.say: A binding check sorts the call by what it touches and where it may run, and marks it runnable only if both are wired.

nodes.title: How a tool runs
nodes.say: Each tool the app calls is bound to a runner: inside Magician, in an operating-system jail, as a governed remote tool, on a device, or refused. Choose one to see it.
nodes.decidedBy: the locked primitive's kind and reviewed skill shape: interactive primitive → device session; MCP-shaped skill → governed MCP; other tool skills → OsJail; compiled tool → InProcessCompiled; a plan that is not runnable → refused

options.label: In-process trusted tool
options.say: A compiled provider built into Magician runs it directly, with reviewed input and result size limits.

options.label: OS jail for an untrusted skill
options.say: A skill from outside runs in an operating-system jail with no network of its own.

options.label: Governed remote MCP tool
options.say: A reviewed remote MCP tool runs through the governed dispatcher that owns checkout, sign-in and spending.

options.label: Browser, Mac or phone session
options.say: An interactive tool drives a browser, a paired Mac or an Android phone under its own session.

options.label: Refused: no working binder
options.say: The tool has no trusted dispatcher for this kind of call, so it is refused before anything runs.

nodes.title: Run in process
nodes.say: A trusted built-in provider runs the call inside Magician, under a one-shot disclosure permit sized to the reviewed byte ceilings.

nodes.title: Prepare the jailed call
nodes.say: The workflow rechecks the locked skill, plans it for the jail, and refuses any action that would need approval or ambient authority.

nodes.title: Run in OS jail
nodes.say: The untrusted skill runs in an operating-system jail on a reserved worker slot, seeing only its staged inputs and working folder.

nodes.title: Egress broker
nodes.say: A per-call broker is the jail's only way out: it allows secure connections to granted public hosts and records every host contacted.

nodes.title: Only granted secrets go in
nodes.say: Only secrets the owner granted this tool are injected, and a required secret that was not granted stops the call before launch.

nodes.title: Governed MCP call
nodes.say: A reviewed remote MCP action goes through the same governed dispatcher as everywhere else, so checkout, sign-in and spending rules still apply.

nodes.title: Ask the owner
nodes.say: When the tool's approval class is above ordinary, the owner is asked to approve this one call, with the amount shown for purchases.

nodes.title: Owner approval
nodes.say: A governed remote tool waits for the owner, who can approve this one call or deny it and let the agent carry on without it. Pick an outcome.
nodes.decidedBy: the owner's answer to the mcp_tool_approval request: approve_once or deny; no answer within 1800 seconds counts as deny

options.label: Approve once
options.say: The owner approves, the remote tool runs once, and its result comes back.

options.label: Deny or no answer
options.say: The owner denies or stays silent for thirty minutes, so the call does not happen.

nodes.title: Run on a device
nodes.say: An interactive tool runs on a browser, a paired Mac or an Android phone, inside a session the owner can watch and stop.

nodes.title: Tool refused
nodes.say: With no trusted dispatcher for this call, the tool is refused before any input leaves, and the agent sees only the refusal.

nodes.title: Result labelled
nodes.say: The result spends the call's disclosure permit and is labelled at a strict local-only floor; no label is ever read from tool output.

nodes.title: The agent's next move
nodes.say: With a tool result in hand, the agent can call another tool or commit its changes and finish the run. Choose which to follow.
nodes.decidedBy: the model's next tool call in the agentic loop: another granted pack, or the terminal app_commit_mutations tool

options.label: Commit and finish
options.say: The agent calls the terminal commit tool to save its changes and end the run.

options.label: Call another tool
options.say: The agent asks the model again and picks another granted tool.

nodes.title: Terminal commit
nodes.say: The terminal commit is checked against the task's own schema and relations, then becomes the run's single final result.

nodes.title: Records written with outbox
nodes.say: Any record changes are written all-or-nothing, and the same transaction appends an entity-change row to the outbox for later delivery.

nodes.title: Client reads the run
nodes.say: The client polls the run handle and gets its status and final result, checked again against the current authority on every read.

nodes.title: Reading or changing data
nodes.say: A client can read a page of the app's records, or commit a change to them. Pick one.
nodes.decidedBy: the public route: QueryData posts an AppQueryRequest, MutateData posts an AppMutationCommand

options.label: Query records
options.say: The client asks for a page of records from the app's own store.

options.label: Mutate records
options.say: The client sends a change that is committed all-or-nothing.

nodes.title: Query the app's store
nodes.say: The query takes its scope from the verified session and the current installation, never from the request, and returns one bounded page.

nodes.title: Records returned
nodes.say: The page of records goes back to the client, marked private and never cached.

nodes.title: Mutate the app's store
nodes.say: The change is fenced by the verified session and an idempotency key, then applied all-or-nothing against the app's current schema.

nodes.title: Outbox row appended
nodes.say: Inside the same transaction, an entity-change row naming the changed records and sequence range is added to the outbox.

nodes.title: Changes reach the screen
nodes.say: A background worker claims outbox rows and broadcasts them as entity-changed events, so open app screens refresh on their own.

nodes.title: App screen updated
nodes.say: The result is on screen, and every step touched only what the owner granted when the app was installed.
